impacts.text: Without a deadline, a user's transaction gives validators a "free option." They can hold the transaction and execute it if and only if it becomes profitable for them (e.g., waiting for market volatility to create a sandwiching opportunity). If it never becomes profitable, they drop it.
Users lose the ability to safeguard their trades against time-based risks.
A transaction intended for specific market conditions can execute long after those conditions have passed (e.g., after a stablecoin de-peg event).
